Subagents, when the capability is available, are an important part of this workflow. Use them as directed by the workflow steps.
If you need an explicit user instruction to run them, ask once now for the whole workflow run.

## Conventions

- Bare paths (e.g. `checklist.md`) resolve from the skill root.
- `{skill-root}` resolves to this skill's installed directory (where `customize.toml` lives).
- `{project-root}`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory.
- `{skill-name}` resolves to the skill directory's basename.

## On Activation

### Step 1: Resolve the Workflow Block

Run: `python3 {project-root}/_bmad/scripts/resolve_customization.py --skill {skill-root} --key workflow`

**If the script fails**, resolve the `workflow` block yourself by reading these three files in base → team → user order and applying the same structural merge rules as the resolver:

1. `{skill-root}/customize.toml` — defaults
2. `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/{skill-name}.toml` — team overrides
3. `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/{skill-name}.user.toml` — personal overrides

Since `@if (konfliktSitzplaetze().length > 0)` renders unconditionally above the `schritt()` checks, the following sequence produces two contradictory messages on screen at once: user hits a seat conflict (banner: "Sitzplatz A1 ist inzwischen belegt.", bumped to step 1) → picks new seats, returns to step 2 → submits again but this time hits a *generic* error (network blip, 500, etc.), which only sets `abschliessenFehler` and does not touch `konfliktSitzplaetze`. The old conflict banner and the new "Die Buchung konnte nicht abgeschlossen werden…" message are now both visible simultaneously on step 2, with the conflict message now referring to seats that are no longer even selected. - **`.buchungsbestaetigung__einzelpreis` is used in the template but never styled.** `buchung.html` renders `{{ position.preisSnapshot | currency: 'EUR' }}`, but the SCSS diff only adds rules for `.buchungsbestaetigung`, `__titel`, `__positionen`, `__position`, `__code`, `__kategorie`, and `__gesamtpreis` — the per-seat price span has no font, color, or layout rule at all and falls back to browser/inherited defaults, breaking visual consistency with its sibling `__code`/`__kategorie` spans in the same row. - **New subscriptions bypass the component's own lifecycle discipline.** The existing `route.paramMap` subscription in the constructor uses `.pipe(takeUntilDestroyed())`, but the two subscriptions added in this diff — `buchungenService.buchungAnlegen(...).subscribe(...)` in `buchungAbschliessen()` and `veranstaltungenService.getSitzplan(...).subscribe(...)` in `aufBuchungsfehlerReagieren()` — are not. If the user navigates away mid-request, these keep running and set signals on a torn-down component, inconsistent with the pattern already established in the same file. - **Seat-plan reload after a conflict has no error handling.** `this.veranstaltungenService.getSitzplan(veranstaltungId).subscribe((neuerPlan) => { this.sitzplan.set(neuerPlan); })` has no `error` handler and no `catchError`. If this secondary fetch fails, it throws an unhandled observable error with zero user-facing fallback — the seat map is left in whatever state it was in, silently, right after the app just told the user their previous selection was stale. - **`ProblemDetails.detail` (and `title`/`status`) are declared but never read.** The interface models an RFC7807-style payload including `detail`, presumably intended to carry a server-provided human-readable explanation, but `aufBuchungsfehlerReagieren` discards everything except `type`/`betroffeneSitzplaetze` and falls back to one hardcoded generic message for every non-conflict error, including cases where the backend may have sent a specific, more useful explanation (e.g. validation failure). - **Non-null assertion on `preiskategorieId` has no runtime guard.** `preiskategorieId: this.kategorieZuordnung().get(code)!` assumes every selected code has an assigned category, but `buchungAbschliessenDeaktiviert` (the gate that enables the submit button) only checks `kontaktName`/`emailGueltig` — it does not re-verify category completeness itself. This line silently depends on an invariant enforced elsewhere (`weiterDeaktiviert`, outside this diff, in step 1). If that invariant is ever weakened or bypassed, this becomes `preiskategorieId: undefined` sent straight to the backend instead of failing fast. - **Clipboard failure is silently swallowed with zero user feedback.** In `Buchungsreferenz.kopieren()`, the `catch` block is empty except for a comment explaining the omission is intentional. If `navigator.clipboard.writeText` rejects — insecure context, denied permission, unsupported browser — the button silently does nothing: no error state, no fallback selection/highlight of the text, no toast. The user is left assuming either the click didn't register or the app is broken. - **Copy confirmation isn't announced to assistive tech.** The button label swap ("Kopieren" → "Kopiert") is a plain text mutation with no `aria-live` region, which is a notable gap given the rest of this diff is careful about ARIA (`aria-live="assertive"` on the conflict banner, `aria-busy` + dynamic label on the submit button). Screen reader users get no confirmation that the copy actually succeeded. - **Hardcoded, non-HTTPS API base URL for a new endpoint that transmits PII.** `BuchungenService` hardcodes `const API_BASE_URL = 'http://localhost:5244'` and posts customer name/email over it. The inline comment ("[ASSUMPTION: gleiche Backend-Basis-URL … kein eigenes Umgebungskonfigurationssystem]") acknowledges the missing environment configuration but ships the duplication anyway instead of centralizing the constant (e.g. re-exporting from `veranstaltungen.service.ts` or a shared config module), doubling the future migration cost. - **No idempotency protection on booking creation.** `BuchungAnlegenRequest` carries no client-generated idempotency/request key. If the POST succeeds server-side but the HTTP response is lost (timeout, dropped connection) and the user retries — which the UI actively allows once `abschliessenLaedt` resets to `false` on error — nothing stops a duplicate booking from being created for the same seats and contact. - **Test pollutes global `navigator.clipboard` without restoring it.** `buchungsreferenz.spec.ts` does `Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'clipboard', { value: { writeText }, configurable: true })` and never removes or restores the original in an `afterEach`/`finally`. Any other spec sharing the same test worker/module context now sees a mocked `navigator.clipboard` that was never cleaned up. - **Potential duplicate `

` on the page.** The new confirmation view introduces `

Buchung bestätigt

` inside what appears to be a sub-section of an existing routed page. Nothing in the diff demonstrates that this route doesn't already render its own page-level `

` elsewhere (e.g. event title), so this risks two `

` elements competing for the document outline. - **Six near-identical `BuchungenService` provider stubs copy-pasted across the spec file.** Every pre-existing `TestBed.configureTestingModule` block in `buchung.spec.ts` gets the exact same line added: `{ provide: BuchungenService, useValue: { buchungAnlegen: () => of(erzeugeBuchung()) } }`. This mechanical, scenario-irrelevant boilerplate is duplicated six times rather than factored into one shared default/helper, adding maintenance surface for something that has nothing to do with what each of those tests is actually verifying. - **Magic number breaks the design-token convention.** `.buchungsbestaetigung__code { min-width: 40px; }` is a hardcoded pixel value sitting in a block where every other declaration in the same diff sources spacing and typography from CSS custom properties (`var(--spacing-*)`, `var(--font-*)`). No equivalent token was reused or introduced. - **No test exercises the per-seat price span.** None of the new specs assert on `.buchungsbestaetigung__einzelpreis` content — which is exactly the element that turned out to have no SCSS rule at all (see above). The missing style rule shipped unnoticed because nothing in the test suite looks at that element.

   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer edge-case JSON with location over adversarial prose).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind+edge`).

3. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.

   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

## Dev Notes

### Bereits etablierte Muster — nicht neu erfinden

- **Eine Route, interne Schritte statt Navigation** (UX-DR10, `EXPERIENCE.md` Zeile 18): Die Buchungsbestätigung ist ein dritter interner Zustand derselben `Buchung`-Komponente (`abgeschlosseneBuchung`-Signal), **keine** neue Angular-Route, kein `Router.navigate`. `app.routes.ts` bleibt unverändert.
- **Signal-State pro Feature, kein globaler Store** — exakt wie die bestehenden `schritt`/`ausgewaehlteCodes`/`kategorieZuordnung`-Signals in `buchung.ts`.
- **`HttpClient`-Service-Muster**: `BuchungenService` folgt 1:1 `VeranstaltungenService` (gleiche `API_BASE_URL`-Konstante, `providedIn: 'root'`, `inject(HttpClient)`).
- **Deutsches Domänenvokabular durchgängig**: `Buchung`, `Buchungsposition`, `Referenz`, `abschliessenLaedt`, `konfliktSitzplaetze`, `buchungAbschliessen` — keine englischen Bezeichner (Architecture Consistency Conventions).
- **Fehlertexte konkret, kein generisches „Ein Fehler ist aufgetreten"** (`DESIGN.md` Do's and Don'ts, UX-DR17) — sowohl die Konfliktmeldung als auch die generische AC-#5-Meldung benennen, was passiert ist bzw. was der Besucher tun kann.
- **Kein Bestätigungs-Icon/-Farbe vor tatsächlichem Servererfolg** (`DESIGN.md` Do's and Don'ts) — die Buchungsbestätigung wird ausschließlich nach dem `next`-Callback des POST-Requests gerendert, nie optimistisch vor Antwort.

### Namenskonflikt `Buchung` (Komponente) vs. `Buchung` (Modell) — zwingend beachten

Die Komponentenklasse in `buchung.ts` heißt `export class Buchung`. Das neue Modell-Interface in `shared/models/buchung.ts` heißt ebenfalls `Buchung` (konsistent mit den anderen unpräfixierten Modellnamen `Sitzplan`, `Preiskategorie`). Der Import in `buchung.ts` **muss** aliasiert werden: `import { Buchung as BuchungDto } from '../shared/models/buchung';` — sonst Compile-Fehler durch doppelte Deklaration im selben Modul-Scope. Das Signal heißt entsprechend `abgeschlosseneBuchung: WritableSignal<BuchungDto | null>`. Im Template (`buchung.html`) ist das kein Problem, da dort kein TS-Namespace existiert — die lokale Template-Variable `buchung` (aus `@if (abgeschlosseneBuchung(); as buchung)`) kollidiert nicht mit dem Klassennamen.

### Backend-Vertrag (Story 2.6, bereits implementiert und getestet — hier nur konsumiert)

- `POST /veranstaltungen/{id}/buchungen` — Request-Body camelCase: `{ name, email, positionen: [{ sitzplatzCode, preiskategorieId }] }`. **Kein Preisfeld im Request** — der Server berechnet den Preis serverseitig (AD-6), das Frontend darf und kann keinen Preis mitschicken.
- Erfolg: `201 Created`, Body ist `BuchungDto` camelCase: `{ referenz, veranstaltungId, name, email, status: "Aktiv" | "Storniert", gesamtpreis, positionen: [{ sitzplatzCode, preiskategorieId, preiskategorieName, preisSnapshot }] }`.
- Konflikt: `409 Conflict`, `Content-Type: application/problem+json`, Body enthält `type: "sitzplatz_belegt"` und Extension-Feld `betroffeneSitzplaetze: string[]` (camelCase, direkt aus `ProblemDetails.Extensions["betroffeneSitzplaetze"]` — keine Naming-Policy-Transformation auf Dictionary-Keys in ASP.NET Core, daher literal camelCase wie im Backend-Code gesetzt).
- Andere Fehler ohne Sonderbehandlung in dieser Story (fallen in AC #5, generischer Zweig): `400` (`preiskategorie_ungueltig`, `sitzplatz_duplikat`), `404` (Veranstaltung nicht gefunden — praktisch nicht erreichbar, da die Seite bereits über dieselbe `veranstaltungId` geladen wurde), `500` (`buchungsreferenz_erzeugung_fehlgeschlagen`), Netzwerkfehler (`status: 0`).
- Quelle: `seed-a-backend.Api/Controllers/VeranstaltungenController.cs` (Action `PostBuchung`), `seed-a-backend.Api/Services/BuchungenService.cs`, `seed-a-backend.Api/DTOs/BuchungDto.cs` — vollständig in Story 2.6 implementiert, unverändert zu übernehmen. Diese Story ändert **keinen** Backend-Code.

### Bekannter, hier bewusst nicht behobener Grenzfall (aus Deferred Work)

`deferred-work.md` (Review von Story 2.5) vermerkt: „`price-summary-bar` bleibt an `ausgewaehlteCodes().size > 0` gekoppelt statt an `schritt()` … wird real relevant, sobald Story 2.7 die Auswahl bei einem Buchungskonflikt eventuell leert, während der Besucher noch in Schritt 2 ist." Mit dem in dieser Story gewählten Design tritt das **nicht** auf: Ein Konflikt setzt `schritt` explizit auf `1` zurück (AC #3), der Besucher befindet sich also nie mehr in Schritt 2 mit geleerter Auswahl. Verbleibt nach einem Konflikt mindestens ein Platz in der Auswahl, bleibt die `price-summary-bar` sichtbar (korrektes Verhalten). Werden **alle** ausgewählten Plätze durch den Konflikt entfernt, verschwindet die `price-summary-bar` vollständig (`ausgewaehlteCodes().size === 0`) — das Konfliktbanner bleibt trotzdem sichtbar und erklärt die Situation; keine AC dieser Story verlangt, in diesem Randfall zusätzlich eine leere Auswahl-UI zu zeigen.
